page: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-3200s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2 instructions. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a 3200 GB local NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong memory performance, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Large-block read and write memory bandwidth tests also show strong results in the top 25%, reaching 340.0 GB/sec and 160.84 GB/sec respectively. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is highly competitive, placing in the top 10%, while multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores align with the average tier. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates strong performance in text generation for small LLM models (135M) at 315.31 tokens/sec, while medium model (7B) text generation and static web serving throughput of 15.74 GB/sec remain in the average range.

This instance offers high resource density, combining a memory-optimized profile with substantial local NVMe storage. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without resource contention, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for workloads requiring large memory footprints and fast local disk access without the premium of specialized bare-metal hardware. The server is well-suited for memory-intensive databases, Redis deployments, large-scale data processing, and local caching applications.
